name_note: The GTDB name matches the literature name; the species is only recently described and most of its literature consists of case reports and identification methods.

sentences.text: Cutibacterium modestum belongs to Cutibacterium, a genus that has been described as skin commensals involved in acne inflammation and occasionally causing healthcare-associated infections.
It is easily missed in the laboratory: mass spectrometry can misidentify it as Cutibacterium acnes, and earlier multiplex PCR assays could not detect it at all.
Published cases include prosthetic valve infective endocarditis and identification in culture-negative pyogenic spondylitis by shotgun metagenomic sequencing.
Finding low-virulence skin commensals of this genus in deep specimens is a diagnostic challenge, because contamination must be distinguished from true infection.
